newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bacob Bank monitors use of information vendors.
newsitem.headline: Bacob Bank monitors use of information vendors.

text.p: Bacob Bank, Belgium's seventh-biggest, said it has started monitoring how and how much its financial markets dealers use news and price information provided by information vendors.

"Our dealers do not see it as a form of control. We just want to know what information we are really using," Bacob board member Walter Vanderbeken said at the presentation of the bank's new dealing room in Brussels' Avenue Livingstone.
Vanderbeken said that Bacob pays about 100 million francs per year to information vendors such as Bloomberg, Reuters and Telerate.
That budget includes write-offs on computer equipment, he said.
"With our new software we can see how many pages are consulted per day," Vanderbeken said.
"We have seen an inflation of information vendors in our dealing rooms. Traders always want more screens. We want to know what we are really using," he added.
In the new trading room, dealers each have a maximum of four screens.
Bacob's new dealing room houses 70 people. Together they produce average daily turnover of about 500 to 600 billion francs.

Bacob invested 40 million francs in a new telephone switching system and new furniture for the dealing room. "This new dealing room is a clear signal from top management that we want to play an active role in professional trading activities," Dirk Vanderschrick, head of financial markets, said.
"In relation to our size, we have a much bigger trading room than other banks," Bacob chief executive officer Dirk Bruneel said.
Bacob's specialties include asset-backed and mortgage-backed securitisation.
